classes: N (normal and bundle branch block beats)

inputs.value: the beat: lead MLII in millivolts after baseline removal; value k is the mean of the two samples at (2k - 90)/360 s and (2k - 89)/360 s from the beat's annotation position (the R peak in most beats), so the window runs from 250 ms before it to about 397 ms after it in steps of 1/180 s and the R peak falls between values 44 and 45
RR before: seconds since the previous beat of the record
RR after: seconds to the next beat of the record
local RR: mean of the up to 10 most recent RR intervals, ending with the one just before this beat (so it includes input 117; fewer near the start of a record)

baseline_removal: the raw MLII signal (360 Hz) minus its baseline, where the baseline is the signal median-filtered with a 200 ms window (71 samples) and then a 600 ms window (215 samples), as de Chazal et al. 2004
aami_classes: N: normal beats, left and right bundle branch block beats, atrial and nodal (junctional) escape beats; S: atrial premature beats, aberrated atrial premature beats, nodal premature beats, supraventricular premature beats; V: premature ventricular contractions, ventricular escape beats; F: fusions of ventricular and normal beats
dataset_facts: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database (Moody and Mark 2001, PhysioNet): 48 half-hour two-lead ambulatory ECG recordings of 47 subjects, 360 Hz, 11-bit over 10 mV, every beat annotated by two or more cardiologists. The four records with paced beats (102, 104, 107, 217) are excluded; the other 44 all have lead MLII. Beats within 250 ms of a record's start or 400 ms of its end, and the first and last beat of each record, are excluded. The held-out beats were drawn at random from all 44 records, so the reference was trained on other beats of the same patients.
forward: h1 = relu(fc1.weight @ x + fc1.bias); h2 = relu(fc2.weight @ h1 + fc2.bias); logits = fc3.weight @ h2 + fc3.bias; the prediction is the argmax (logits within 1e-9 x max(1, |max logit|) of the maximum count as tied; ties go to the lowest index)
metric: balanced accuracy: the mean, over the four classes, of the share of that class's held-out beats predicted correctly; 2,850 held-out beats (1,000 N, 600 S, 1,000 V, 250 F)
